_doc: Role-default WAKE POLICY table (sealed 2026-09-22, pair 3566adb5): what a
woken crown may run WITHOUT a human to confirm it. This is a stand-in for
the real source — the seat's own signed manifest, surfaced through
session_enter by willow-mcp (not built here; see the build packet's
'no broker changes' rule) — used whenever session_enter's response does
not itself carry an explicit wake_policy key.
Bash is absent from every entry on purpose and ratatosk.wake_policy.load()
refuses to load a table that names it anywhere: Kart is the shell, never
a wake. A role missing from this table means a wake for that role refuses
to start — a silent empty policy would be an unbounded one, not a narrow
one.
'allow' only matters for a tool whose verdict would otherwise prompt a
human (today: Bash, Write, Edit — PolicyStore's own default confirm
rules). Everything else (Read, and every MCP verb the seat's manifest
grants — task_submit among them) already resolves to ALLOW under the
existing permission gate and is listed here for readability, not because
listing it changes anything: the manifest gate still decides which MCP
verbs exist for the seat at all; this table only decides which of
crown's own local confirm-class tools may run unconfirmed.
write_scope 'packet_worktree' additionally requires Write/Edit's target
path to resolve under the worktree the packet's own assignment names;
null means Write/Edit are refused outright for that role (no scope to
confine them to).
